answer:
The newest release notes covering LFM3 (v0.40.13) say the models run on Linux and Windows as well as Apple silicon:

"Liquid AI's [LFM3](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3) models, including text-to-speech in [lfm3-audio](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-audio) and [lfm3-omni](https://ollama.com/library/lfm3-omni), now run on Linux and Windows as well as Apple silicon." [ollama/v0.40.13.md]

This supersedes the earlier v0.40.12 note, which limited support to Apple hardware: "Note: lfm3 and d1 2b are supported on Apple hardware in this release. Support for Linux/Windows coming soon." [ollama/v0.40.12.md]

So as of 0.40.13, LFM3 runs on Apple silicon, Linux, and Windows. The v0.40.13 note names the LFM3 models only. It does not say whether d1 2b (also built on LFM3) got the same expansion, so I don't know that from this context.
